reply.title: At the Highest Point
reply.story:
When you toss a ball straight up into the air, it slows down as it climbs, pauses for a brief fraction of a second at its highest point, and then speeds up on its way back down. Watching it hang motionless at the very top, it is tempting to think that everything stops—that both its speed and its acceleration drop to zero.

Galileo grappled with this exact puzzle when studying falling bodies. If the acceleration were zero at the apex, the ball would feel no force and would stay suspended up there rather than turning around. By looking closely at how velocity changes smoothly from positive to negative, we can see that the pull of gravity never lets up, even at the exact instant the velocity passes through zero.
reply.cardDescription: Explore the vertical throw where velocity passes through zero at the apex, while acceleration remains constant at $-g$.
reply.instructions: Press play to watch the throw. Adjust the launch speed and gravity to see how the apex time and height change.
